ratings.reason: The quote explicitly defines a persistent left–center–right decomposition and binds each panel to global/chat actions, graph editing, or selected-node details. It is an unusually clean structural match, although the practical impact of the layout itself cannot be isolated from the limited evidence.

Three named panels are assigned distinct design functions, strongly supporting the pattern. The quote does not give positions, permitted interactions, or establish whether all panels remain simultaneously visible, so implementation and impact are only moderately clear.

The quote enumerates four regions, assigns each a stable role, and distinguishes browsing, editable sketching, reference selection, and output display. That editability asymmetry and apparent workflow ordering make this a particularly complete exemplar.

The evidence plainly specifies left, middle, and right regions for participants, communication, and idea visualization. The division enables complementary coordination activities, though a sidebar–chat–visualization arrangement is not especially novel.

This is an explicit three-column layout with stable left navigation, central authoring, and right assistance roles. It clearly separates the primary editable artifact from navigation and AI support, although the arrangement is fairly conventional.

The quote fixes four components in left-to-right order and gives each a recognizable function. It strongly supports spatial decomposition, but says little about interaction details, persistence, or why this partition changes outcomes.

The paired 3D explorer and rich-text editor have clearly distinct, stable exploration and typing functions, including an editability distinction. Their precise spatial relationship and persistence are not stated in the quote.

Four named components are tied to data, commands, the working artifact, and dynamically synthesized controls. The fixed functional frame accommodating changing widgets is a strong, transferable instance of content changing within a stable regional role.

Left, center, and right regions have distinct roles, but the central panel can be collapsed, weakening the pattern's persistence requirement. The quote also does not explain what the Cluster panel does.

The quote gives a stable top–middle–bottom partition for controls, upcoming chords, and performance input. Spatial order directly supports the temporal music interaction, although that particular composition is more domain-specific than most candidates.

A PDF viewer with left and right panes is structurally suggestive, but the quote names the side panes without stating their functions or interactions. It therefore demonstrates the partition more clearly than the functional binding central to the pattern.

The quote directly assigns reading and discussion to persistent left and right panels. The separation plausibly supports material-grounded discussion and transfers well, though it is a familiar split-view design and interaction detail is sparse.

Three named workspaces separate prompting, digital design preview, and physical-output preview, producing a legible input-to-production workflow. Positions and persistence are not stated, and the clay-print partition is domain-specific.

The evidence explicitly defines three left-to-right panels for ideation, metric exploration, and impact/risk assessment. The spatial partition also encodes a useful evaluation progression, making it more purposeful than a generic panel layout.

The two-row organization binds the top to source/algorithm outputs and the bottom to configuration and haptic previews. This is a clear functional decomposition with an input/output relationship, but its pane count and exact interactions are underspecified and domain-bound.

The quote enumerates five stable-looking views for input, image evidence and scoring, 3D output, text exploration, and keyword contribution. Functional roles are clear, but concurrent placement and persistence are not explicitly established.

The quote labels several interface elements and a heat map, but does not establish that they form a fixed set of persistent regions; some are merely selection options. It is related evidence, but weaker than explicit panel or workspace decompositions.

Document, Notebook, and Table views are each bound to a distinct scale or function: source reading, document-level actions, and collection overview. This is highly transferable, although the quote does not explicitly state their positions or simultaneous persistence.

Six named components divide a writing environment among artifact creation, AI functions, simulated feedback, attribution, and character information. The roles are substantive, but the quote provides neither spatial arrangement nor explicit persistence, limiting confidence in the exact pattern.

Input, analysis, and report-writing regions support a clear prompt-to-audit-to-document workflow, with distinct interaction permissions. The quote labels regions A–C but does not state their screen positions or persistence explicitly.

Five named views divide data, topics, chart editing, composition, and recommendations into separate functions. The structure is clear and reusable, but the quote does not specify spatial arrangement, persistence, or detailed interaction behavior.

Four sections assign space to the essay, visual synthesis, feedback, and revision, plausibly supporting a coherent revision workflow. The quote names rather than explains the regions, so position, persistence, and permissions remain uncertain.

The quote cleanly divides the interface into an editable text region and a dedicated metaphor-support region, with explicit activities in each. This is a strong and broadly transferable artifact-plus-assistance split, though structurally conventional.

The quote specifies a left–middle–right composition for collaboration, shared policy editing, and private model experimentation. The public/private and shared/private asymmetry is an unusually purposeful use of fixed regions that materially enables simultaneous coordination and safe individual testing.

Reference, spatial-authoring, results, and history components have distinct roles spanning input, creation, output, and provenance. The quote does not provide their positions or explicitly confirm persistent coexistence, so it falls short of the cleanest exemplars.

Four views separate raw data, narrative, visualization, and design controls, a clear functional partition supporting several aspects of visualization authoring. Spatial placement and region-specific interactions are not supplied in the quote.

The evidence assigns validation overview, detailed data, and rule settings/cards to named views, but it is unclear whether these are simultaneous persistent regions or switchable application views. The truncated quote further limits confidence in the complete layout.

The quote lists search, moodboard, metadata, and image-generation functions, which could form a fixed functional workspace. It does not call them panels or views, give their positions, or establish stable regional identity, so the structural signature is only partially demonstrated.

The quote explicitly places video on the left and timed captions, descriptions, and feedback in right-side table columns. This clearly binds source media and multiple aligned authoring/feedback functions to persistent regions, though the design is relatively conventional.

Three explicitly named panels separate task framing, conversational search, and a persistent collection of claims selected for verification. The partition supports deliberate transfer from dialogue to scrutiny and is readily reusable beyond this study, although outcome evidence is unavailable here.
